openers: Read together, your fifty answers say this: you
Your answers point clearly in one direction — you
Your answers keep pointing the same way: you
Taken together, your answers show that you
matchLead: The reason {name} comes first is that you
{name} is where you end up because you

compare.better: Where it fits you better than {primary}: you
compare.shared: What it shares with you: you
compare.apart: The widest gap: it leans "{it}", you lean "{you}".
compare.further: The widest gap: it goes further towards "{it}" than you do.
compare.beyond: The widest gap: you are more "{it}" than it is.

tension: You are also more "{side}" than a typical fan of {name}, and that is what makes your version your own.

high: look for places where nature is in charge
like a place better the more plants and animals live there
low: feel best in places that are fully built and tidy
don't need nature around you to feel well

high: prefer materials that live and change
like surfaces that carry the marks of time
low: like clean, stable surfaces that stay put
like things that are man-made and predictable

high: want a field or a forest close by
see living far from the neighbours as a good thing
low: need something larger than a village around you
want things within easy reach

high: come alive in cities and movement
enjoy a city the way other people enjoy a view of nature
low: get little out of the pace of a city
stay away from busy places

high: are genuinely curious about how machines work
think technology can be beautiful
low: keep technology at a distance
trust things that don't need electricity

high: have a real relationship with what happens on a screen
remember places in games and online as well as real places
low: want things in your hands, not in an app
feel screens take more than they give

high: look ahead rather than back
like the thought that everything could be different
low: don't believe new always means better
look for answers in what already exists

high: find beauty in things built for work
like steel, concrete and visible structure
low: stay away from things that are hard and machine-like
want soft things where others are fine with steel

high: choose places with a past over places without one
see a story in old buildings and objects
low: don't feel bound by what came before
live in the present without missing anything

high: miss times that are gone
are moved by signs of how people used to live, even strangers
low: don't see the point in missing the past
throw things out without feeling sad about it

high: are drawn to the look of decades before your own
like things that clearly look old-fashioned
low: want things to look like their own time
don't like new things made to look old

high: value traditions and doing things the same way over time
like that something is done because it always has been
low: don't care much how things are usually done
would rather find your own way than inherit one

high: like things that are new, clean and work well
want things that don't carry someone else's wear
low: like things that show their age more than things that look perfect
avoid things that are too new and too smooth

high: like it best when something stays unexplained
are drawn to things that are half hidden
low: want answers rather than atmosphere
aren't very drawn to mysteries

high: keep one foot in worlds that don't exist
think in pictures more than in facts
low: stay with what actually is
have little need for invented worlds

high: want things that are real over things that are pretty
care about what works and what is true
low: care more about mood and feeling than about plain facts
would rather have the beautiful than the correct

high: find something good in sadness
like beauty with sorrow in it
low: keep away from sad and heavy things
are drawn to things that are light and easy

high: believe that things usually turn out well
are mostly in a good mood
low: don't expect the world to get much better
see the shadows before you see the light

high: are at home in low light and long shadows
like darkness as atmosphere, not as threat
low: need light around you
avoid dark and gloomy things

high: have kept your playful side
like the strange and the unpredictable
low: take things seriously
have little patience for the silly

high: draw energy from other people
want people around you
low: are drained by too much company
need fewer people than most

high: want to belong to something larger than yourself
value having a role among others
low: manage perfectly well without a group
keep a little outside the group

high: need time alone to feel whole
enjoy being by yourself
low: rarely seek solitude
would rather have someone in the room

high: would rather stand out than fit in
want to decide for yourself, even when it is hard
low: don't need to stand out
are comfortable doing as others do

high: feel calm with routines and order
want things to have their place
low: live perfectly well with disorder
feel trapped by too many rules and systems

high: work best when things are allowed to be a bit messy
trust the unplanned
low: want control over how things unfold
don't like things happening by accident

high: want fewer but better things around you
feel free in an empty room
low: need things around you to feel at home
would rather fill a room than empty it

high: want rooms full of things that mean something
collect rather than clear out
low: keep the number of things you own low
feel uneasy when there is too much stuff

high: value things somebody actually made
would rather do it yourself
low: have little need to make things yourself
would rather buy it finished

high: think detail and decoration make things better
like something being decorated for no reason at all
low: want it bare and undecorated
see decoration as clutter

high: put warmth and shelter first in your surroundings
want places to sink into
low: are fine with a simple, bare life
give up comfort when it gets in the way of other things

high: get restless staying in one place too long
want to see what's around the next bend
low: are at your best at home
don't need adventure to be content

high: notice things that are elegant and well made
notice when something has been done properly
low: prefer things that are rough and unpolished
don't care for things that are too polished

high: want to understand things thoroughly, not just experience them
like to study and learn about the world
low: trust instinct over analysis
have little need to study what you like

high: notice rooms, light and buildings before you notice people
pay close attention to buildings
low: care little how buildings look
barely notice the room you're in

setting.text: and it sits far enough out that nobody passes by
and there is always somebody there — the place only works with people in it
in the middle of something that still has traffic and light all night
preferably in grey weather, when all the colours look soft and faded
and you rarely stay long enough to put down roots
with something warm within reach the whole time

architecture.text: though in your version everything stands straight and square
in your version it is extended, patched and never quite finished
and you notice every detail — how the roof meets the wall, where the light gets in
and the building was something else before it was yours
with only the parts it really needs
with extra decoration nobody needed, but you love anyway

interior.text: and every surface is covered in something you have collected
with few things, none of them accidental
and half of it is inherited or found
and you made or mended several of them yourself
lit from low lamps, never from the ceiling
and everything is chosen so people can stay sitting

technology.text: and you understand how it works, not just how to use it
and you keep it to a minimum
with at least one screen always on in the background
and the screens lie face down
and what you own, you can repair
and you want the newest version before it is finished

clothes.text: and the clothes say plainly that this is you
but with nothing that asks for attention
always a bit more dressed up than you need to be
and it has to take hard wear
and nothing you cannot sit in for hours
with at least one detail there purely because it is nice

music.text: mostly in a minor key, and usually for a little too long
and preferably something with lift in it
and best of all with other people in the room
played on an old format, like vinyl or cassette
and it can happily be uneven and badly recorded

colours.text: but several shades darker than the standard version
in a lighter version than people expect
and all of them at once
though only two of them — the rest stays neutral
always with earthy or plant colours underneath
with one completely unreasonable colour allowed in

everyday.text: and all of this happens without an audience
and most of it is done alongside somebody
at roughly the same time every day
with no particular plan, which is the whole point
with a book or a question left open the whole time
until you suddenly decide to go somewhere
